transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42m
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Rajesh Kumar (Celestial Head of Infra), Sofia Alvarez (Celestial Cloud Architect), Tom Benson (Celestial Partnerships)

Summary:
- Introductory partner discovery between Redwood Inference and Celestial Compute.
- Discussed possible integration patterns (marketplace/reseller, dedicated GPU pools, private deployments), security posture, and initial pilot scope (latency benchmarks, VPC peering).
- Agreed next steps: send deck/pricing, schedule technical deep dive, customer to share network/topology info.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Maya from Redwood - i'm the AE on this. Um, quick intros, Ethan is our solutions engineer.
[00:07] Ethan: Hey all.
[00:09] Rajesh: Rajesh here, thanks for setting this up. We're interested in partner programs and, uh, how Redwood could fit into our offering for customers who need low-latency inference.
[00:18] Tom: Tom from partnerships, yes, exploring reselling and integration options.
[00:22] Sofia: Sofia, cloud architect - i'll be more technical here.
[00:25] Maya: Great. Goal for today is to understand Celestial's infra, go through high-level integration models (hosted API vs dedicated vs private), and surface security/compliance questions. Also see if there's immediate POC interest.
[00:36] Rajesh: Cool. Quick background: we run a managed GPU hosting business across multi-region POPs, mix of A100 and next-gen custom cards, customers range from startups to telco. We want to offer inference as a service with partners like Redwood to avoid building our own serving layer. Main asks: predictable latency SLAs, cost profile, and how we can bundle Redwood as a managed offering.
[00:54] Ethan: Awesome, that aligns. Redwood typically supports three modes - hosted (Redwood API), Dedicated (reserved pools, SLA-backed), and Private (VPC/on-prem). For partners we often do a reseller or co-managed dedicated offering. For Celestial, it sounds like dedicated or private would be most relevant.
[01:10] Sofia: A few constraints: our customers often require VPC peering, KMS integration (customer-managed keys), and SOC2/ISO audit artifacts. We also need to know about data residency and how audit logs are surfaced.
[01:22] Maya: Totally, those are common. We have KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, SOC2, and enterprise support. For private deployments we can integrate into customer VPC and support customer KMS. For Dedicated we provide isolation + reserved capacity.
[01:34] Rajesh: How have you handled KV cache and batching? Some of our retail customers care about token-level latency, they can't tolerate big batching delays.
[01:44] Ethan: Good Q - our runtime supports continuous batching and prefix/KV caching and you can tune batching windows. For latency-sensitive routes we configure lower batching thresholds and enable KV cache to speed prompt prefix retrieval. There's always a trade-off cost vs latency, but we expose levers.
[01:57] Tom: On commercials - do you have partner discounts / revenue share for ISPs and resellers?
[02:02] Maya: Yes, we have partner pricing and reseller programs - we'll share the partner deck/pricing sheet after this call.
[02:07] Sofia: From a networking perspective, we need to understand egress patterns and whether Redwood's control plane needs inbound access to our management plane.
[02:15] Ethan: For Private deployments, control plane can be customer-managed and we support limited outbound-only control plane comms; specifics depend on air-gap needs. For Dedicated and Hosted, we have secure tunnels and peering options. We can share our network diagram.
[02:28] Rajesh: Benchmarking - we'd want a quick POC showing latency at 1k QPS with 8k context for our LLM customers. Is that something you can run on our stack?
[02:39] Ethan: We can - typically we run a POC where we deploy a compatible model variant, run synthetic load, and collect latency percentiles. We may need access to a dev image or a test cluster in Celestial to run infra-native tests.
[02:51] Maya: Also worth discussing quantization and model selection. Are you offering instance types customers prefer for 7B vs 70B?
[02:59] Rajesh: We run multiple instance types; we want to know Redwood's recommendations for quantization and kernel optimizations.
[03:05] Ethan: Our Optimize product will suggest quantization profiles and kernel selection based on model arch and sequence length distribution. For partners we can include those recommendations in the onboarding docs.
[03:15] Sofia: Security questions: SSO/SAML for console, RBAC, and audit retention windows. We have enterprise customers who require 7 years of logs (ugh).
[03:24] Maya: RBAC and SSO/SAML supported, audit retention is configurable with add-on retention tiers; 7 years is long - we'll raise with product but we can provide exports and long-term storage options.
[03:35] Tom: Any competitors or similar partnerships we should be aware of?
[03:38] Maya: There are a few, we often hear about Velascale and PinnacleGPU in the partner/reseller space, and some cloud providers building inference stacks.
[03:46] Rajesh: Pricing model - do you do per-token plus reserved capacity?
[03:50] Maya: Hosted is usage-based (per-token / per-embedding). Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commits. For resellers we have partner pricing tiers. We'll share concrete numbers in the pricing sheet.
[04:02] Sofia: One tricky item is multi-tenant customers who need tenant-level isolation inside the same cluster - do you support multi-tenant isolation primitives?
[04:11] Ethan: Yes we have per-route isolation, model pinning, and can map tenants to dedicated routes or namespaces. For stronger isolation we recommend dedicated pools per tenant.
[04:20] Rajesh: Operational questions - how do you handle rollouts and canary testing?
[04:23] Ethan: Our console supports rollouts, canary deploys, A/B tests, and automatic fallback policies to keep apps online if a model regresses.
[04:31] Tom: Integration patterns - we can either list Redwood as a marketplace offering on Celestial, or embed a managed Redwood instance for customers. Which is easier to get started?
[04:40] Maya: Quickest is to list Redwood-hosted API in marketplace - minimal infra work. If you want a managed offering with Celestial-branded experience, Dedicated/Private is the path but takes more setup.
[04:52] Rajesh: For pilots, timeline wise, we want a demo + tech-deep-dive next week and pilot by the end of the month if numbers look good.
[05:00] Maya: Sounds reasonable. We'll schedule a technical deep dive with Ethan.
[05:03] Ethan: For the tech-deep-dive we'll ask for sample workload characteristics: avg sequence length, percent of streaming responses vs batch, expected qps, and whether customers require function-calling or structured outputs.
[05:14] Sofia: I'll share those details - also security questionnaire and sample topology.
[05:17] Rajesh: How about legal / procurement - do you have standard reseller agreement or do we need to route through legal?
[05:23] Maya: We have standard partner agreements; for enterprise deals legal review is typical. We can share an NDA and partner term sheet.
[05:29] Tom: Ok great. Anything else?
[05:31] Maya: Quick recap: Maya to send partner deck + pricing; Ethan to run benchmarks for dev cluster once we get access; Celestial to share VPC/topology and workload stats; schedule tech deep-dive next week.
[05:45] Rajesh: Perfect, thanks everyone.
[05:48] Maya: Thanks, we'll follow up in email - sending notes and links.

References/Artifacts mentioned:
- Partner deck & pricing sheet (link: notes/docx - will be sent by Maya)
- Redwood security & SOC2 docs (link: security.redwood.example/doc)
- Network/topology questionnaire (link: to be shared by Sofia)

End of transcript.
